text:
deploy-bot: kickoff: rolling model-service v2.3.1 to production (region-by-region). Schedule: US -> EU -> APAC. Canary in US first, then staged ramp. See playbook: https://confluence.redwood/internal/deploys/v2.3.1 :rocket:

alex: starting US canary now. 2 small nodes, target 5% traffic, 10m soak. will run smoke script: `smoke/us_canary.sh`

deploy-bot: canary-started: region=us target=5% nodes=2 canary_id=cb-3600001111

sre-jen: quick checklist: watch p95, p99, 5xx rate, GPU mem OOMs, queue-depth. Alert thresholds we agreed: p95>300ms for 3m OR 5xx>0.8% for 5m -> hold/rollback. Also watch region thermal events.

maria: adding route-pin fallback for enterprise customers pre-emptively. If we see regressions, we pin enterprise orgs to v2.2.4 to avoid blast radius. Command: `redwoodctl route pin --org=enterprise --version=v2.2.4`

dan: noted. ops: please make sure reserved warm pool for EU is at 120% capacity before we cutover there. EU has a nightly billing job at 01:50 UTC; prefer to delay EU rollout until after 03:00 UTC to avoid contention.

iris: logging smoke run here:
```
# smoke/us_canary.sh
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d @payload.json | jq '.choices[0].text'
# ramp to 200 qps over 5m, hold 5m
```

deploy-bot: canary-result: region=us p95=128ms p99=310ms 5xx=0.17% errors=0.24% gpu_util=62% mem_used=74% -> PASS (within canary gates) :white_check_mark:

alex: good. starting staged ramp in US to 25% over next 20m. will monitor for hold triggers.

sre-jen: reminder - if p99 > 800ms OR sustained GPU mem > 92% on more than 1 node -> escalate and consider rollback. Also watch KV-cache hit rate drop (prefix cache miss could spike CPU).

maria: deploying config to enable fallback routing when model queue_length > 150: `routing.max_queue=150 fallback.version=v2.2.4`

ops-bot: reserved-warm-pool-check: us=OK (150/150), eu=75/120 (warmups pending), apac=60/80.

alex: decision: hold EU until 03:10 UTC for warm pool to finish, then EU canary at 10% for 15m. APAC will be last, low-traffic window at 10:00 UTC+8.

dan: adding explicit rollback triggers to release notes for oncall:
- if p95 > 400ms for 5m -> rollback to v2.2.4
- if 5xx > 1% for 5m -> rollback
- if sustained GPU OOM or node crash -> rollback and open incident
Rollback command: `redwoodctl rollout abort --to-version=2.2.4 --region=$REGION`

iris: EU canary started at 03:12 UTC (we had a 2m warmup delay). initial telemetry: p95=160ms p99=420ms 5xx=0.3% gpu_util=58%

deploy-bot: eu-canary-log snippet:
```
[03:13:05] canary cb-3600001111-eu: success probe=200/200 latency_avg=145ms p95=162ms errors=0.28%
[03:20:00] ramping to 25%
```

sre-jen: small note: one EU node showed elevated GC pause ~200ms on midnight indexing job. not correlated to model service yet but keep eyes open.

maria: pinging enterprise eng to confirm pin rollback command is ready in case we need immediate per-org pinning.

ops-bot: eu warm pool post-ramp: 120/120 -> OK.

alex: APAC schedule pushed 30m earlier due to local partner demo. we'll keep APAC ramp conservative: 5% canary -> 10% -> 20% with manual approvals between steps. oncall to ack before each step.

dan: logging release notes snippet to releases board and sent to #product-notes. Added metrics to watch and rollback steps.

iris: quick check-in: no errors >1% anywhere, tail latencies holding. I'll leave an open thread for 60m to capture any regressions.

maria: FYI, if we have to rollback, preference is graceful fallback -> pin sensitive routes -> then full rollback. reduces customer disruption.

alex: +1. tagging @oncall for heads up. If anyone sees anything odd, call it out and we'll hold ramp.

ops-bot: final: rollout proceeding. timeline: US -> EU -> APAC. manual gates at each 25% ramp. remember to update incident channel if rollback triggered. :thumbsup:

sre-jen: thanks all. will keep monitoring and post if thresholds hit.

maria: :pray:

alex: closing the thread unless something pops up.
